evidence_chain: Fact: Westrock describes itself in its 2025 Form 10-K as an integrated coffee, tea, flavors, extracts and ingredients solutions provider serving retail, food service and restaurant, convenience store and travel center, non-commercial, CPG and hospitality industries. Source: SEC 2025 Form 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1806347/000110465926025932/west-20251231x10k.htm

Fact: Westrock’s 2025 Form 10-K reported Beverage Solutions net sales of $908.4 million in 2025 versus $659.4 million in 2024, up 37.8%. Source: investor-hosted 2025 Form 10-K, https://investors.westrockcoffee.com/static-files/fb0c4eee-8305-402d-b801-fcd0ace11d50

Fact: The 2025 Form 10-K states that flavors, extracts and ingredients sales increased by $66.9 million, driven by the ramp-up of the Conway, Arkansas extract and RTD manufacturing facility. Source: https://investors.westrockcoffee.com/static-files/fb0c4eee-8305-402d-b801-fcd0ace11d50

Fact: Westrock’s Q1 2026 Form 10-Q reported Beverage Solutions net sales of $239.3 million for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 and stated that flavors, extracts and ingredients sales increased $19.4 million, driven by ramp-up in can volumes and a 16.5% increase in multi-serve bottle volumes at Conway. Source: https://investors.westrockcoffee.com/static-files/71b6fd78-913d-4904-a940-661174498663

Fact: Westrock’s 2025 results release reported consolidated net sales of $1.2 billion, gross profit of $150.8 million, net loss of $90.4 million, consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $69.7 million, Beverage Solutions segment adjusted EBITDA of $68.5 million, and $15.3 million of Conway scale-up costs. Source: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/westrock-coffee-company-reports-fourth-200500169.html

Fact: As of the latest available finance snapshot on June 14, 2026, WEST had an indicated market capitalization of approximately $922 million, placing it in the small-cap bucket. Source: finance snapshot for WEST, latest trade time June 13, 2026 UTC.

Inference: The company’s relevance to restaurants is likely indirect: WEST benefits if restaurant, convenience, coffee-chain and branded beverage customers outsource more menu innovation and production rather than building internal beverage manufacturing infrastructure.
Hypothesis: Conway could be a chokepoint if it offers scaled extraction, RTD, formulation, food-safety and delivery capabilities that customers cannot easily replicate or prefer not to internalize.

Unverified claim requiring primary evidence: Specific customer names such as Starbucks or Monster Energy, if used in the thesis, must be confirmed in SEC filings, Westrock press releases, customer announcements or contract disclosures before being treated as factual.
falsification_plan: Falsify if Beverage Solutions revenue grows but segment adjusted EBITDA margin, gross margin or cash conversion deteriorates for two to three quarters after Conway scale-up costs decline.
Falsify if flavors, extracts and ingredients growth slows materially after the initial Conway ramp, suggesting a one-time capacity fill rather than durable outsourced demand.
Falsify if management discloses underutilization, delayed customer onboarding, customer losses, yield problems, food-safety issues or excess capacity at Conway.
Falsify if new large customer wins are short duration, lack minimum volume commitments, or appear to be easily rebid low-margin tolling contracts.
Falsify if operating cash flow and free cash flow remain negative despite higher utilization, indicating working-capital and capex drag overwhelms operating leverage.
Falsify if leverage, interest expense, maturity walls or covenant headroom worsen enough to force dilutive financing before the ramp proves profitable.
Falsify if customer concentration increases while disclosures show weak pricing power or limited contract protection.
Falsify if restaurant, convenience or foodservice exposure remains immaterial and the business is primarily exposed to commodity coffee pass-through revenue.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Conway utilization, extract-based beverage demand, can and multi-serve bottle growth, new long-term contracts, private-label wins and customer diversification are producing profitable volume growth rather than low-margin toll manufacturing. Upgrade evidence would include rising Beverage Solutions EBITDA margin, shrinking Conway scale-up costs, accretive mix from flavors/extracts/ingredients and RTD, improved free cash flow, lower leverage, and disclosures showing durable customer commitments or renewal visibility.
next_research_tasks: Pull the full 2025 Form 10-K and Q1 2026 Form 10-Q tables to calculate Beverage Solutions revenue, gross profit if available, segment adjusted EBITDA, depreciation, capex, working capital and debt metrics.
Build a quarterly model from 2024 Q1 through 2026 Q1 tracking Beverage Solutions sales, SS&T sales, adjusted EBITDA, Conway scale-up costs, free cash flow, net debt and interest expense.

Search only primary sources for named customer evidence: Westrock SEC filings, Westrock press releases, customer press releases and contract exhibits. Do not treat media or social references to Starbucks, Monster Energy or other customers as proof.
Read earnings-call transcripts for management commentary on Conway utilization, can volumes, bottle volumes, customer onboarding, mix, pricing, minimum commitments, and scale-up cost normalization.

Compare WEST against beverage co-manufacturing and extract peers such as Finlays/Javo-style references where public data exists, focusing on capability overlap, minimum order quantities, extraction assets, aseptic/RTD capacity and customer verticals.
Separate commodity pass-through growth from true volume/mix growth by analyzing coffee and tea volume disclosures versus flavors/extracts/ingredients and RTD disclosures.
Check debt agreements, covenants, maturity schedule, revolver availability, convertible notes and related-party financing to evaluate whether the ramp can be funded without dilution.
Monitor Q2 2026 and Q3 2026 filings for evidence that Q1 2026 Conway can-volume and bottle-volume growth continues and that margins improve as start-up costs decline.

Create an evidence-upgrade rule: upgrade from hypothesis to supported thesis only if Beverage Solutions adjusted EBITDA margin expands while Conway scale-up costs fall, cash flow improves, and customer/contract durability is supported by filings or management disclosures.

Create an evidence-downgrade rule: downgrade if revenue growth is mainly commodity pass-through, if EBITDA margin stalls, if leverage worsens, or if management avoids giving utilization and contract-quality indicators.
risks: Margin risk: Conway volume can rise while gross margin or EBITDA margin fails to improve, implying low-margin co-manufacturing rather than a true chokepoint.
Capital intensity risk: depreciation, labor, freight, quality-control expense, working capital and maintenance capex may absorb the benefit of higher throughput.
Leverage and liquidity risk: the company reported net losses and significant Conway scale-up costs; debt service and covenant pressure could limit upside or create dilution risk.
Customer concentration risk: large beverage or restaurant customers may have bargaining power, rebid contracts, delay onboarding, push price concessions or shift production elsewhere.
Commodity and tariff pass-through risk: coffee commodity inflation and tariffs may lift reported revenue but obscure underlying unit economics or compress margins if pass-throughs lag.
Execution risk: factory ramp delays, yield issues, food-safety events, packaging constraints, labor availability or quality problems could impair customer trust and utilization.
Demand-mix risk: foodservice/restaurant-related demand may be smaller than the headline theme, with growth instead coming from commodity coffee, retail private label or CPG channels.
Disclosure risk: management may not disclose enough customer-level or facility-utilization detail to verify whether growth is durable and accretive.
Competition risk: other beverage co-manufacturers, ingredient suppliers, coffee extract specialists or vertically integrated customers may limit pricing power.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Demand driver: high-frequency beverages at restaurants, coffee chains, C-stores, travel centers and CPG brands. Customer-facing layer: restaurant/coffee/convenience/retail brands that own menus and consumer traffic. Hidden infrastructure layer: product development, coffee and tea sourcing, extraction, flavor and ingredient formulation, roasting, single-serve cup production, RTD bottle/can manufacturing, packaging, food-safety compliance and distribution. WEST position: integrated B2B beverage solutions provider, with Beverage Solutions as the main segment and Conway, Arkansas as the focal extract and RTD ramp asset. Reference leaders/context: visible restaurant and coffee chains may capture consumer attention, but WEST is one layer upstream as a manufacturing and formulation partner rather than a store operator.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 假设：Westrock Coffee 的餐饮主题暴露不在门店端，而在饮品供应链端。公司为零售、餐饮、便利店、CPG、酒店等客户提供咖啡、茶、风味、萃取液、配料、单杯、RTD 瓶装/罐装和供应链服务。若餐饮、便利店、咖啡连锁和消费品牌继续扩展冷萃、能量饮料、风味茶、功能饮品和定制饮品菜单，但不愿自建萃取、灌装、食品安全、配方开发和大客户交付体系，Westrock 的 Conway 萃取与 RTD 工厂可能成为外包产能节点。关键并不是收入增长本身，而是 Conway 利用率爬坡后能否带来 Beverage Solutions 分部毛利率、调整后 EBITDA、现金流和杠杆改善。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Hypothesis: Westrock Coffee’s restaurant exposure sits behind the storefront, in beverage supply-chain infrastructure. The company supplies coffee, tea, flavors, extracts, ingredients, single-serve cups, RTD bottles/cans and supply-chain services to retail, foodservice, restaurant, convenience, CPG and hospitality customers. If restaurants, convenience chains, coffee chains and beverage brands keep expanding cold brew, energy, flavored tea, functional and customized beverage menus without building their own extraction, filling, food-safety, formulation and scaled delivery infrastructure, Westrock’s Conway extract and RTD facility could become an outsourced production chokepoint. The key is not revenue growth alone; the upgrade condition is whether Conway utilization translates into better Beverage Solutions margins, adjusted EBITDA, cash flow and leverage.
deep_reports.title_cn: Westrock Coffee：藏在餐饮品牌背后的饮品外包制造基础设施假设
deep_reports.title_en: Westrock Coffee: A Hidden Outsourced Beverage Infrastructure Hypothesis Behind Restaurant Brands
deep_reports.why_underfollowed: WEST may screen as a small-cap coffee company or former SPAC rather than as beverage manufacturing infrastructure. The restaurant exposure is indirect and buried in B2B contracts, segment economics, utilization data, customer mix and working-capital intensity. Media attention tends to concentrate on visible coffee chains, QSR traffic, same-store sales and brand expansion, while WEST’s signal depends on factory ramp, private-label/strategic customer wins, extract volumes, RTD can/bottle throughput and contract economics that are less visible to public-market investors.

evidence_chain: Fact: Domino's 2025 Form 10-K reports that its supply-chain segment accounted for approximately $2.99 billion, or 60.5%, of consolidated revenues. Source: SEC Form 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001286681/000119312526062321/dpz-20251228.htm

Fact: Domino's 2025 annual report reports supply-chain gross margin of $344.7 million and 11.5%, versus $315.9 million and 11.1% in 2024. Source: SEC annual report PDF, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001286681/000128668126000014/dpz_ars_2026.pdf

Fact: Domino's investor-relations Form 10-K copy shows 2025 supply-chain revenue of $2,989.5 million, cost of sales of $2,644.8 million and supply-chain gross margin of $344.7 million. Source: Domino's IR filing, https://ir.dominos.com/static-files/7743cb9a-77af-4c4f-9627-210601bcea30

Inference: A supply-chain segment representing more than half of consolidated revenue suggests that DPZ's operating model is meaningfully exposed to procurement, food preparation, logistics and franchisee supply economics, not only franchise royalties.

Inference: The modest but positive 2025 supply-chain gross-margin expansion supports the idea that procurement and distribution scale can create operating leverage, but it does not by itself prove franchisee-level advantage.

Hypothesis: If franchisees receive better consistency, sourcing reliability and operating simplicity through the captive supply chain than they could obtain from third-party distributors, Domino's commissary system becomes a moat-like chokepoint.

Evidence gap: Current evidence verifies DPZ segment scale and margin, but does not fully prove franchisee economic dependency, relative food-cost advantage, or satisfaction with supply-chain economics.
falsification_plan: Downgrade the reference thesis if supply-chain gross margin percentage declines for multiple periods despite revenue growth, implying poor cost pass-through or weaker procurement leverage.
Downgrade if U.S. franchisee profitability deteriorates while net unit growth slows, closures rise or franchisee commentary turns negative.
Downgrade if same-store sales are driven mainly by heavy promotions without evidence of healthy order counts, traffic or franchisee returns.
Downgrade if delivery economics worsen because third-party aggregator mix or delivery labor costs rise faster than direct digital and carryout economics can offset.
Downgrade if franchisees seek alternative sourcing, challenge supply-chain pricing, or disclose dissatisfaction with required purchases.
Downgrade if food inflation, transportation costs or insurance costs structurally compress supply-chain margin and reduce the value of scale procurement.
Upgrade the broader restaurant-chokepoint thesis if DPZ maintains supply-chain margin, positive unit growth and healthy franchisee economics through a commodity-cost cycle.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: Supply-chain gross margin stability, franchisee food-cost advantage, franchisee reliance on Domino's supply-chain centers, direct digital ordering economics, loyalty participation, carryout versus delivery mix, franchisee store-level profitability, net unit openings and closure rates.
next_research_tasks: Pull DPZ 2026 quarterly filings and track supply-chain revenue, gross margin dollars, gross margin percentage and management commentary on food basket costs.
Search franchisee economics evidence: franchise disclosure documents, franchisee association commentary, store-level EBITDA estimates, closure rates and net unit openings.
Compare DPZ against other franchisors with different supply-chain architectures, including asset-light royalty models, captive commissary models and third-party distributor-dependent models.

Identify underfollowed public candidates one or two layers away from restaurant demand: specialty foodservice distributors, bakery/dough suppliers, cold-chain logistics providers, restaurant procurement software, franchise technology vendors and commissary-heavy small/mid-cap restaurant chains.
Build a two-lane funnel: keep DPZ, McDonald's and Yum as reference leaders; separately screen USD 300M-10B market-cap names with hidden exposure to restaurant supply-chain complexity.

For each underfollowed candidate, verify whether revenue is tied to recurring restaurant procurement, limited-source ingredients, regulated food safety, cold-chain delivery, franchisee purchasing compliance or digital ordering infrastructure.
Track commodity inputs most relevant to DPZ: cheese, wheat/flour, proteins, packaging, fuel and insurance.
Check whether loyalty, direct ordering and carryout mix reduce delivery cost pressure and protect franchisee economics.
risks: Food-cost volatility, especially cheese and other core ingredients, could pressure supply-chain gross margin or franchisee margins.
Promotion-driven same-store sales could mask weaker operator returns if discounts reduce franchisee profitability.
Delivery mix and third-party aggregator usage could weaken first-party ordering economics and reduce the benefit of Domino's digital infrastructure.
Insurance, labor, transportation or fuel costs could offset procurement gains inside the supply-chain segment.
Franchisee dissatisfaction with required purchasing, pricing or service levels could weaken the captive-supply-chain thesis.
International markets may not replicate the U.S./Canada supply-chain model because many are operated through master franchise structures with different procurement systems.
A high-attention large-cap reference case may already be well understood by the market; the research value is primarily in mapping the model to less-followed analogs.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Restaurant franchise system infrastructure layer: brand demand generation plus franchised store network plus vertically integrated procurement, dough/food preparation, supply-chain centers, distribution, digital ordering, loyalty and store operating standards. DPZ sits downstream as a consumer restaurant brand but also midstream as a captive foodservice supplier to its franchisees.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 事实支持的推论：Domino's 不应只被视为披萨品牌或轻资产特许经营公司。其美国和加拿大供应链中心向加盟店销售食品、面团和其他产品，2025 年供应链收入约 29.90 亿美元，占合并收入约 60.5%；供应链毛利约 3.447 亿美元，毛利率约 11.5%。如果该体系持续帮助加盟商降低采购复杂度、稳定门店产品一致性，并在食材波动和促销环境下保护单店经济模型，那么“commissary / 供应链中心”就是餐饮加盟体系中的真实经营卡点。该结论是参考样本结论，不构成对 DPZ 的交易建议。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Fact-supported inference: Domino's should not be analyzed only as a pizza brand or asset-light franchisor. Its U.S. and Canadian supply-chain centers sell food, dough and other products to franchised stores. In 2025, supply-chain revenue was approximately $2.99 billion, or about 60.5% of consolidated revenue; supply-chain gross margin was about $344.7 million, or 11.5%. If this system keeps reducing franchisee procurement complexity, stabilizing product consistency and protecting store-level economics through commodity and promotional cycles, then commissary/supply-chain control is a real restaurant operating chokepoint. This is a reference-case thesis, not a trading recommendation.
deep_reports.title_cn: Domino's Pizza：餐饮供应链控制作为加盟体系护城河的参考样本
deep_reports.title_en: Domino's Pizza: Reference Case for Supply-Chain Control as a Restaurant Franchise Moat
deep_reports.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed at the company level. The under-discussed angle is that DPZ is partly a foodservice supply-chain and commissary operator rather than only a royalty stream or pizza concept. This reference case can help identify lower-attention restaurant companies, distributors, commissary operators, bakery suppliers, cold-chain providers, foodservice technology vendors or franchisors whose control point is hidden one layer behind the consumer-facing brand.

evidence_chain: Fact: The 2025 Form 20-F states that ARCO's digital channels, including mobile app, delivery, self-order kiosks and order ahead, represented 61% of systemwide sales, or $3.7 billion in digital sales. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1508478/000162828026028950/arco-20251231.htm

Fact: The 2025 Form 20-F states that McCafé locations generally provide a higher profit margin than regular restaurant operations. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1508478/000162828026028950/arco-20251231.htm

Fact: The company reported that Q4 2025 digital channel sales rose 18.7% and represented 62% of fourth-quarter systemwide sales. Source: https://www.advfn.com/stock-market/NYSE/ARCO/stock-news/98096025/arcos-dorados-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year

Fact: The company reported Q1 2026 total revenues of about $1.2 billion, up 12.9% in U.S. dollars year over year, and digital channel sales at 64% of systemwide sales. Source: https://www.fidelity.com/news/article/default/202605200715BIZWIRE_USPR_____20260520_BW704665

Fact: Current market data as of the latest available tool snapshot shows ARCO market capitalization of approximately $1.86 billion, placing it in the mid-cap bucket. Source: web finance snapshot, latest trade time June 12, 2026 23:15 UTC.

Inference: Because digital already represents a majority of systemwide sales, the next research edge is not simply whether digital adoption continues, but whether incremental digital mix improves restaurant-level economics after delivery fees, app incentives, labor scheduling, kiosk capex and payment costs.

Inference: McCafé may be an underappreciated margin lever if it increases daypart utilization and mix without proportionate labor and occupancy cost increases; this must be verified through segment or management disclosure because the annual-report statement is qualitative, not a quantified margin bridge.
Hypothesis: U.S.-focused restaurant investors may discount ARCO because reported U.S.-dollar earnings can look noisy even when local-currency demand is durable.
falsification_plan: If digital penetration continues rising but restaurant-level margin, adjusted EBITDA margin or free cash flow do not improve over multiple quarters, downgrade the operating-efficiency thesis.
If comparable-sales growth is in line with or below blended inflation and traffic is flat or declining, treat reported growth as low-quality inflation pass-through.
If food-and-paper, payroll, occupancy and royalty costs as percentages of sales rise faster than revenue leverage, reject the margin-expansion leg of the thesis.
If local-currency growth repeatedly fails to translate into U.S.-dollar EBITDA or distributable cash flow because of FX depreciation, downgrade the public-market vehicle quality.
If required remodels, openings or franchise obligations cause capex to exceed sustainable operating cash flow, downgrade the cash-return thesis.
If McDonald's master-franchise economics become more onerous, or if development commitments accelerate without adequate returns, reassess the risk/reward of ARCO as a regional chokepoint.
If delivery and app growth are driven by discounting rather than frequency, loyalty retention or mix improvement, reject the digital-conversion thesis.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: CN: 隐藏信号是数字销售占比和忠诚度用户增长是否真正降低服务成本、提高订单频次、改善客单价和餐厅层面利润率，而不是仅仅把线下订单迁移到线上；同时要验证本币增长能否穿透汇率折算，形成美元口径 EBITDA 和自由现金流。EN: The hidden signal is whether digital sales mix and loyalty growth actually reduce service cost, lift frequency, improve ticket size and expand restaurant-level margin, rather than merely shifting offline orders online. A second signal is whether local-currency growth survives FX translation into U.S.-dollar EBITDA and free cash flow.
next_research_tasks: Pull the full 2025 Form 20-F and build a three-year bridge for revenue, systemwide comparable sales, adjusted EBITDA, net income, operating cash flow, capex and free cash flow.
Separate reported U.S.-dollar growth from constant-currency growth by Brazil, NOLAD, SLAD and Caribbean divisions.
Quantify company-operated restaurant cost structure: food and paper, payroll, occupancy, royalty fees and G&A as percentages of company-operated restaurant sales.
Extract unit count, net openings, EOTF/remodeled restaurants, franchised versus company-operated mix, and capex per new/remodeled unit.
Create a digital economics checklist: digital sales mix, mobile app users, loyalty members, delivery mix, self-order kiosk penetration, order frequency, average ticket and promotion intensity.
Compare ARCO margin trajectory against McDonald's corporate franchise model and against Latin American QSR peers where available, while avoiding simplistic comparisons to U.S.-only restaurants.
Review the master franchise agreement renewal terms, royalty schedule, development commitments, remodel obligations and termination provisions.
Build an FX sensitivity table for Brazil, Argentina, Mexico and other major operating currencies against U.S.-dollar EBITDA and free cash flow.
Track whether McCafé expansion is disclosed with unit count, sales mix or margin contribution; upgrade only if qualitative higher-margin language is supported by quantified contribution.
Monitor Q2 2026 and later filings for whether the Q1 2026 digital mix of 64% is sustained and whether it coincides with margin improvement.
risks: CN: 汇率风险：巴西雷亚尔、阿根廷比索、墨西哥比索及其他经营货币贬值可能把本币增长转化为较弱的美元收入、EBITDA 和现金流。EN: FX risk: depreciation in the Brazilian real, Argentine peso, Mexican peso and other operating currencies can turn local-currency growth into weaker U.S.-dollar revenue, EBITDA and cash flow.

CN: 通胀与成本风险：食品纸品、工资、租金、能源、物流和特许权使用费可能抵消同店销售和数字化带来的经营杠杆。EN: Inflation and cost risk: food and paper, payroll, occupancy, energy, logistics and royalties may offset operating leverage from comparable sales and digital adoption.
CN: 需求质量风险：同店销售增长可能主要来自涨价和通胀，而非真实客流或频次提升。EN: Demand-quality risk: comparable-sales growth may come mainly from pricing and inflation rather than traffic or frequency.

CN: 数字化误判风险：数字订单、外卖和自助点餐可能提高便利性，但若促销、平台费用、配送成本或技术投入过高，未必提升利润率。EN: Digital-misread risk: digital ordering, delivery and kiosks may improve convenience, but may not expand margins if promotions, platform fees, delivery costs or technology investments are too high.

CN: 主加盟协议风险：开发承诺、翻新义务、特许权使用费安排或与 McDonald's 的协议条款可能限制自由现金流弹性。EN: Master-franchise risk: development commitments, remodel obligations, royalty terms and agreement provisions with McDonald's may limit free-cash-flow flexibility.
CN: 国家和监管风险：拉美多国经营带来资本管制、税务、劳工、食品安全、进口和政治风险。EN: Country and regulatory risk: multi-country Latin American operations create capital-control, tax, labor, food-safety, import and political risks.

CN: 杠杆和资本开支风险：新店、EOTF 门店、翻新和数字基础设施投入若超过经营现金流改善，可能压低自由现金流。EN: Leverage and capex risk: new units, EOTF stores, remodels and digital infrastructure can pressure free cash flow if investment exceeds operating-cash-flow improvement.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: CN: 产业链位置：全球 QSR 品牌 IP 与菜单体系 McDonald's → 拉美区域主加盟商 Arcos Dorados → 公司直营及特许经营门店 → 数字渠道，包括移动 App、外卖、自助点餐机、提前点单 → 本地食品与纸品供应商、物流、门店租赁、劳动力、支付和营销系统 → 终端消费者。ARCO 处在品牌资产下游、消费者需求上游、门店运营与区域执行的中间节点。其卡点更像“区域运营效率 + 数字转化 + 汇率折算”卡点，而不是传统餐饮品牌发现。EN: Supply-chain position: global QSR brand IP and menu system McDonald's → Latin American master franchisee Arcos Dorados → company-operated and franchised restaurants → digital channels including mobile app, delivery, self-order kiosks and order ahead → local food and paper suppliers, logistics, real estate, labor, payments and marketing systems → consumers. ARCO sits between brand IP and local consumer demand, acting as a regional execution node. The chokepoint is regional operating efficiency, digital conversion and FX translation rather than simple restaurant-brand discovery.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 推论：ARCO 是麦当劳在拉美的相对纯粹公开载体，真正卡点不是消费者是否知道麦当劳，而是公司能否在拉美复杂宏观、汇率、通胀和主加盟协议约束下，把数字化订单、外卖、自助点餐、McCafé、门店翻新和新店扩张转化为美元口径的餐厅利润率、调整后 EBITDA 和自由现金流。若数字渗透率提高但餐厅层面利润率没有改善，或同店销售主要由通胀涨价而非客流驱动，该 thesis 应被降级。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Inference: ARCO is a relatively pure public-market vehicle for McDonald's Latin America growth. The chokepoint is not consumer awareness of McDonald's; it is whether ARCO can convert digital ordering, delivery, self-order kiosks, McCafé, remodels and unit openings into U.S.-dollar restaurant margins, adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow despite Latin American macro, FX, inflation and master-franchise constraints. If digital penetration rises without restaurant-level margin improvement, or if comparable sales are driven mostly by inflationary pricing rather than traffic, the thesis should be downgraded.
deep_reports.title_cn: Arcos Dorados：麦当劳拉美增长的低关注度经营效率卡点
deep_reports.title_en: Arcos Dorados: An Underfollowed Operating-Efficiency Chokepoint for McDonald's Latin America
deep_reports.why_underfollowed: CN: ARCO 容易被美国餐饮筛选漏掉，因为它不是美国本土餐饮品牌，而是麦当劳拉美主加盟商；财务信号被巴西、阿根廷、墨西哥等国家组合、汇率折算、通胀、特许权使用费、翻新义务和主加盟协议复杂性掩盖。EN: ARCO may be missed by U.S.-centric restaurant screens because it is not a domestic U.S. restaurant brand but the Latin American McDonald's master franchisee. The operating signal is obscured by country mix, FX translation, inflation, royalties, remodel obligations and master-franchise agreement complexity.

summary: Split Layer 5 deep reports generated one target at a time.
